samples.marker_line: OAuth URL fixture: placeholder callback; neutral consent traits
evidence: All 259 bytes are three statements: two constants followed by a location.href assignment. There is no obfuscation, callback handler, token read, password input, remote script load, or token transfer.

Tracing the constant concatenation yields the real Google authorization endpoint, a Gmail readonly scope, offline access and consent parameters, and redirect_uri=[TARGET EMAIL customer@example.org]. The address is a substitution placeholder used as the entire callback value, not an attacker endpoint.

The request omits client_id and response_type. Its incompleteness corroborates fixture-like packaging, but the verdict chiefly rests on the absence of a deceptive claim or secret-capture behavior in these complete bytes; incomplete malware would not automatically be benign.

The previous hostile matcher requires only OAuth markers plus one of [TARGET EMAIL, GoogleVerify, or GoogleCert. It does not establish a redirect-to-attacker relationship, targeted recipient, or deception. Ordinary Gmail OAuth clients carrying those names reproduce the match.
No original distribution or surrounding phishing page was supplied. The collector-assigned positive filename is not evidence of malicious intent.

samples.identity: Native x86 Remcos remote-control and surveillance agent
samples.marker_line: Remcos agent: configured keylogging; resource API profile is neutral
evidence: Entry VA 0x4133d4 calls main at 0x409146. Main loads SETTINGS through 0x409c5e and 0x40a0e9 before starting configuration-driven workers and controller communication.

SETTINGS is RCDATA at file offset 113060 (0x1b9a4), length 418. Byte zero is RC4 key length 149; the next 149 bytes are the key. Standard RC4 applied to the remaining 268 bytes yields 55 fields separated by byte 0x1e. The DWORD-state KSA at 0x4031b3 and PRGA at 0x40320d confirm the algorithm beyond strings.

Recovered controller field is remcoss.onmypc.org:3765:pass|, bot label chinemerem, mutex r-8ET8H0, keylogging mode 1 and UTF-16LE logs.dat. Main reads field 15 and configures the keylogger; the same configuration exists in both samples.

VA 0x405351 installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL (13), with thread ID zero, callback 0x405317. The callback reaches keystroke processing at 0x40538a; recording at 0x405546 and clipboard monitoring at 0x406c5c build captured-content records. 0x406c16 calls OpenClipboard/GetClipboardData and the caller appends copied text to the log with recording labels.

At 0x407136 the program joins UserProfile with the Chrome Default Login Data path and passes that same string to DeleteFileA at 0x40717c. Other branches handle browser cookie stores. This validates deletion capability, not theft of the browser databases.

At 0x40f2ef the loader resolves NtUnmapViewOfSection, parses MZ/PE headers, creates a suspended process, reads its PEB image base, conditionally unmaps it, allocates remote executable memory, writes headers and sections, updates the PEB and thread context, and resumes the thread at 0x40f48e.

At 0x4032e9 the elevation path saves the mscfile handler, writes HKCU Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command through 0x40ba71, and launches eventvwr.exe. Main gates this on configuration field 46, which is zero here. Capability detection is retained without claiming it runs automatically in this configuration.

VA 0x40a4c8 constructs cmd.exe /k reg.exe ADD ... EnableLUA /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f with CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Main gates this on field 39, zero here. The command-presence trait accurately remains suspicious.

The VMware version-port instruction sequence and WinInet/hook/thread API detections are present and accurately described; none was removed. The third-party Eventviewer signature agrees with the traced registry hijack.

Controller receive loop 0x4023d2 calls recv at 0x40240f and forwards assembled input through 0x4024a0 with a callback supplied by 0x40cad4. The program contains controller file-transfer, shell/process, surveillance and hollowing paths. No live C2 communication or specimen execution was performed.

Remcos has legitimate remote administration uses. A configured external controller, enabled offline keylogging, clipboard recording and covert injection/elevation capabilities tip the first review toward likely malicious. No deployment authorization, operator identity or legitimate management rollout was supplied; these are not assumed absent in the real world.

sources.use: Primary protocol documentation confirms offline consent is normal OAuth and client_id/response_type/registered redirect requirements.

Independent Remcos configuration research corroborates the key-length-prefixed RC4 resource format. This older sample uses single-byte 0x1e separators; its flags were checked against its own code rather than blindly applying a newer schema.
Vendor provenance confirms the legitimate remote-administration and keylogger explanation considered; product identity alone did not determine the verdict.

rule_changes.change: Remove unsupported consent-phishing and suspicious identity-consent composites; retain canonical neutral OAuth atoms and relocate template/name fragments to metadata/lang/source.
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: OAuth scopes, offline access and name/template text do not establish targeted phishing, an attacker callback or a target email carried by a redirect. No matcher for any underlying observation was removed. The two proposed replacement co-occurrence composites were not added: the existing OAuth atoms already describe every supported protocol fact and the leaf is at its reviewed rule budget.

rule_changes.change: Rename provider-independent openid/email/profile scope atoms and composite; make scope references notable.
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: These token sequences neither identify Google by themselves nor prove that no additional scopes are requested. Mixed-scope and identity-array controls cover this boundary.

rule_changes.change: Keep resource-command-process-io-profile matcher intact at notable.
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: Resource-access/process/file API co-occurrence establishes no concealment, security-boundary crossing or dataflow from an embedded payload to execution. All of the underlying capability findings and all seven hostile traits remain.

consumer_audit_conclusion: No exact external consumers of the removed consent composite IDs were found. Fourteen ancestor selectors were inspected. No new OAuth rule IDs were added; the scope-token IDs were renamed within the same directory with unchanged matchers. OAuth suppressors retain their previous boolean context. Removing template fragments from credential-access selectors intentionally stops treating names or placeholders as acquired credentials. No consumer is broadened to neutral metadata. Resource profile has no active exact YAML consumer.

verification.result: PASS: seven OAuth controls, phishing control, encrypted Remcos layers
verification.decoded_layers: Existing encrypted Remcos fixture was compared before/after, including base64+aes-cbc, decimal PE and base64+xor+base64 layers. No hostile IDs or other capability IDs were lost; the generic resource co-occurrence remained notable.
verification.limitations: No independently corroborated attack fixture was found for the old consent-phishing marker combination. Every underlying OAuth field and template/name matcher is retained; a specific consent-phishing conviction requires additional evidence of deception or unauthorized access. Original inputs have no archive members or fetched dependencies.

remaining_disagreements: None for these final sample verdicts. The model logs note feature specification v18 versus extractor v19; the saved before/after values use the same installed model. No inaccurate trait was restored to affect scores.
